name: São Toméan Calulu
description: Calulu is genuinely São Tomé and Príncipe's national dish - real technique traditionally soaks dried fish overnight to rehydrate before it goes into the pot, and the real, patient version can simmer up to five hours; real palm oil, okra, eggplant, and spinach together are what define it, not a quick weeknight stew.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Fish, tuna, light, canned in water, drained solids
ingredients_full.note: standing in for real dried, rehydrated fish

ingredients.ingredient: Fish, tuna, light, canned in water, drained solids
ingredients.note: standing in for real dried, rehydrated fish

steps_detailed: Cook the onion and garlic in the palm oil, 3-4 minutes.
Add the eggplant and jalapeño, and simmer 12-15 minutes until the eggplant is nearly tender.
Add the fish and okra, and simmer 10-12 minutes.
Add the spinach and simmer 5-8 minutes more until wilted - real calulu traditionally simmers far longer than this for full depth, given the time to do so.

name: São Toméan Molho de Cacau
description: Molho de cacau, a real sweet-savory sauce made from cocoa, genuinely reflects São Tomé's identity as one of the 'Chocolate Islands' - real cocoa pulp isn't a distinct item here, so unsweetened cocoa powder stands in, missing the fresh pulp's real bright, fruity tang.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in a little oil, 3-4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 8-10 minutes.
Whisk in the cocoa powder and honey, and simmer 5 minutes more, balancing real sweet against real savory.

name: São Toméan Feijoada Santomense
description: Feijoada santomense, a real bean stew with pork, adapts the Portuguese classic with local beans and real palm oil, a beloved dish for social gatherings and celebrations.

steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion in the palm oil, 6-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cowpeas with a splash of water, and simmer 20-22 minutes until well combined.

name: São Toméan Funge
description: Funge, a smooth cassava or plantain starch, is the real, traditional accompaniment to calulu, real technique beating the flour into boiling water gradually to keep it smooth.

ingredients_full.note: boiled and mashed, standing in for cassava flour

ingredients.note: boiled and mashed, standing in for cassava flour

steps_detailed: Boil the cassava until completely soft, 20-25 minutes.
Mash and beat vigorously until smooth and cohesive.

name: São Toméan Blablá
description: Blablá, mashed breadfruit, is a genuine island side dish - real breadfruit isn't a distinct item here, so yam stands in for a similarly starchy, mashable texture.

ingredients_full.note: peeled and cubed, standing in for breadfruit

ingredients.note: peeled and cubed, standing in for breadfruit

steps_detailed: Boil the yam until completely soft, 20-22 minutes.
Mash until smooth.

name: São Toméan Peixe Assado
description: Peixe assado, whole grilled fish seasoned simply with lime and salt, is a real, ubiquitous coastal dish across the islands.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the lemon juice and salt, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.
steps: Rub the fish with the lemon juice and salt, and let sit 10 minutes.

name: São Toméan Arroz Doce de Coco
description: Arroz doce de coco, a real coconut rice pudding, is a beloved, simple island dessert, reflecting genuine Portuguese culinary influence.
steps_detailed: Simmer the rice with the coconut milk and sugar, stirring often, 20-25 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Dust with cinnamon before serving.
steps: Simmer the rice with the coconut milk and sugar, stirring often, 20-25 minutes, until thick and creamy.

name: São Toméan Pão Doce
description: Pão doce, a real sweet bread, reflects genuine Portuguese baking tradition and is found in bakeries across the islands.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour, sugar, softened butter, baking powder, and egg with a little water into a soft dough.
Shape into a small round loaf and bake at 350F (175C) for 20-22 minutes until golden.

name: São Toméan Fried Breadfruit
description: Fried breadfruit is a common island snack - real breadfruit isn't a distinct item here, so plantain stands in for a similarly starchy fried snack.
steps_detailed: Fry the plantain slices, turning, 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp at the edges.

name: São Toméan Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common home cooking across São Tomé and Príncipe.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.
